Question Choices: Twelve students are divided into labeled teams A, B, and C of sizes 2, 5, and 5. What is the probability that two specified students are on the same team?
Hints: Count pairs of positions within each team;Use [C(2,2)+C(5,2)+C(5,2)]/C(12,2)
Solution: There are $C(12,2)=66$ possible pairs of positions.;The favorable count is $C(2,2)+C(5,2)+C(5,2)=1+10+10=21$.;Thus the probability is $21/66=7/22$.

Question Choices: Fifteen students are divided into labeled teams A, B, and C of sizes 4, 5, and 6. What is the probability that two specified students are on different teams?
Hints: First count same-team position pairs;Use C(4,2)+C(5,2)+C(6,2);Subtract the same-team probability from 1
Solution: The same-team probability is $[C(4,2)+C(5,2)+C(6,2)]/C(15,2)=(6+10+15)/105=31/105$.;Therefore the different-team probability is $1-31/105=74/105$.

Question Choices: Fourteen students are divided into labeled teams A, B, and C of sizes 4, 4, and 6. How many divisions place two specified students together on team C?
Hints: The two specified students already occupy two team C places;Choose the other 4 C members from 12 students;Then choose 4 of the remaining 8 for team A
Solution: Choose the remaining $4$ members of team C in $C(12,4)$ ways.;Then choose team A in $C(8,4)$ ways, with team B determined.;The count is $C(12,4)C(8,4)=495\cdot70=34650$.

Question Choices: Eighteen students are divided into three labeled teams of size 6. What is the probability that four specified students are all on the same team?
Hints: Treat the four students as occupying 4 of 18 team positions;There are C(18,4) possible position sets;Each of three teams contributes C(6,4) favorable sets
Solution: There are $C(18,4)=3060$ possible position sets.;The favorable count is $3C(6,4)=3\cdot15=45$.;Thus the probability is $45/3060=1/68$.
